description: A redirect manifest defines all URL redirects for the site: source URLs, destination URLs, and HTTP codes — enforced to ensure no loops, chains, or broken routing before deployment.

rules.description: A redirect-manifest.spec.json must exist with a redirects array. Each entry needs 'from' and 'to' fields.
No redirect may point back to a URL already in its own redirect path. Loops cause infinite redirect errors in all browsers.
A redirect destination may not itself be a redirect source (A→B where B→C is also defined). Chains add latency and violate HTTP semantics.
Status codes must be 301 (permanent move), 302 (temporary move), or 410 (gone). Other codes are not valid redirect semantics. 410 must have no 'to' destination.
from and to URLs must differ after trailing slash normalization. A self-redirect is an infinite loop.
URLs must start with '/' unless crossDomain:true is set. Absolute URLs in a site redirect manifest indicate a configuration error.
